title: How do you get there?
grammar: How do you get there? — by + transport; prepositions of place
pair_game: Point at a picture. Ask: “How do you get to school?” Your partner answers “By …”. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: How do you get there?
grammar_box.tip: by bus, by car, by metro — BUT on foot and I walk.

questions: How do you get to school every day?
Do you walk to school or take the bus?
What time do you leave home for school?
Is your school far from your home?
How do your parents go to work?
Where is the nearest park from your house?
What time does your school start?
Do you take the bus or subway?
Describe the way from your home to school.
starters: I get to school by … . / I go on foot.
I … to school. It takes about … minutes.
Yes, it is far. / No, it is near — only … minutes.
My mother/father goes to work by … .
Yes, I ride a bicycle … . / No, I cannot ride one.
The nearest park is … from my house.
I take the … . / I do not take the bus or metro.
First I … . Then I … . Finally I … .
samples: How do you get to school every day?
I get to school **by bus**. The stop is near my house, so it **takes** only fifteen minutes.
Is your school far from your home?
No, it is quite near. I go **on foot** and it **takes** about ten minutes.
Describe the way from your home to school.
First I walk to the bus stop. Then I go **by bus** for four stops. Finally I walk two minutes to the gate. On the way I see the market and a big park.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: How do you get to school?

game.title: Roll and travel!
game.rules: Roll the dice. Say two sentences about that transport. Your group says “Good!” or asks a question.

mini_talk.title: My journey to school
plan: Say how you get to school
Say what you see on the way
mini_talk.model: I live in a flat near the park. Every morning I leave home at half past seven and I get to school **by bus**. The stop is in front of my house and the journey **takes** about twenty minutes. On the way I see the market, a mosque and my friend's house. When the weather is good I go **on foot** with Jasur.
